title: Physiological information processing, not genetic hardware, dominates cancer outcomes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Physiological information processing, not genetic hardware, dominates cancer outcomes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin interprets the ability to normalize oncogene-driven tumours by restoring bioelectric connectivity (reinflating cells' cognitive light cone) as showing that physiological information processing, not genetic hardware, dominates cancer outcomes, suggesting a clinical roadmap different from chemotherapy.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Cancer and the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This ability to reinflate the cognitive light cone of cells shows that physiological information processing, not genetic hardware, dominates outcomes and suggests a clinical roadmap quite different from the chemotherapy that dominates the field today [165, 168, 182].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Cancer and the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Cancer in animals, with clinical implications for humans

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.47

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public cancer resources can compare genetic and physiological correlates and test restricted intervention responses. They cannot support the sweeping dominance conclusion or clinical implication without matched causal trials across heterogeneous cancers.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across cancer models, compare outcome variance explained and causal rescue achieved by physiological-state interventions versus genotype, stratifying by tumour type and mutation. Consistent normalization despite persistent driver mutations would support a restricted dominance claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Dominates outcomes is undefined across cancer types.

Observational clinical data confound genotype and physiology.

Xenopus normalization does not establish a human therapeutic roadmap.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The dominance claim is testable once bioelectric state and genotype are measured on the same outcomes, but no public resource contains both. Genomic cancer archives can describe genetic associations and cannot show that physiological information processing outweighs them. The frog intervention papers do not fill that gap as open data, so the claim needs new or newly deposited measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Partition tumor outcome variance between measured bioelectric connectivity and genotype in the same subjects, or compare normalization by restoring connectivity against normalization by correcting the oncogene. Physiological variables explaining more outcome than genotype would support dominance; the reverse would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Dominance is a quantitative comparison that a narrative reading of either literature cannot settle.

Public cancer cohorts measure mutations and expression, not tissue-scale bioelectric state.

The Xenopus rescue experiments are not a deposited dataset and do not cover clinical outcomes.
